arxiv-2107-08273.title: STRODE: Stochastic Boundary Ordinary Differential Equation
arxiv-2107-08273.creator: Hengguan Huang, Hongfu Liu, Hao Wang, Chang Xiao, Ye Wang
arxiv-2107-08273.description: Abstract Perception of time from sequentially acquired sensory inputs is rooted in everyday behaviors of individual organisms. Yet, most algorithms for time-series modeling fail to learn dynamics of random event timings directly from visual or audio inputs, requiring timing annotations during training that are usually unavailable for real-world applications.

arxiv-2205-12990.title: How to renormalize coupled cluster theory
arxiv-2205-12990.creator: Z. H. Sun, C. A. Bell, G. Hagen, T. Papenbrock
arxiv-2205-12990.description: Abstract Coupled cluster theory is an attractive tool to solve the quantum many-body problem because its singles and doubles (CCSD) approximation is computationally affordable and yields about 90% of the correlation energy. Capturing the remaining 10%, e.g. via including triples, is numerically expensive.

arxiv-2207-09097.title: Lazy Estimation of Variable Importance for Large Neural Networks
arxiv-2207-09097.creator: Yue Gao, Abby Stevens, Rebecca Willet, Garvesh Raskutti
arxiv-2207-09097.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Yue Gao, Abby Stevens, Rebecca Willet, Garvesh Raskutti. As opaque predictive models increasingly impact many areas of modern life, interest in quantifying the importance of a given input variable for making a specific prediction has grown. Recently, there has been a proliferation of model-agnostic methods to measure variable importance (VI) that analyze the difference in predictive power between a full model trained on all variables and a reduced model that excludes the variable(s) of interest.

arxiv-2301-00189.title: Mapping Knowledge Representations to Concepts: A Review and New Perspectives
arxiv-2301-00189.creator: Lars Holmberg, Paul Davidsson, Per Linde
arxiv-2301-00189.description: Abstract The success of neural networks builds to a large extent on their ability to create internal knowledge representations from real-world high-dimensional data, such as images, sound, or text. Approaches to extract and present these representations, in order to explain the neural network’s decisions, is an active and multifaceted research field.

arxiv-2302-03064.title: Investigating Pulse-Echo Sound Speed Estimation in Breast Ultrasound with Deep Learning
arxiv-2302-03064.creator: Walter A. Simson, Magdalini Paschali, Vasiliki Sideri-Lampretsa, Nassir Navab, Jeremy J. Dahl
arxiv-2302-03064.description: Abstract Ultrasound is an adjunct tool to mammography that can quickly and safely aid physicians with diagnosing breast abnormalities. Clinical ultrasound often assumes a constant sound speed to form B-mode images for diagnosis. However, the various types of breast tissue, such as glandular, fat, and lesions, differ in sound speed. These differences can degrade the image reconstruction process.

arxiv-2303-05056.title: Hadamard matrices of order 36 36 formed by codewords in some ternary self-dual codes
arxiv-2303-05056.creator: Masaaki Harada, Keita Ishizuka
arxiv-2303-05056.description: Abstract In this note, we study the existence of Hadamard matrices of order 36 36 formed by codewords of weight 36 36 in some ternary near-extremal self-dual codes of length 36 36 . Keywords: Hadamard matrix, ternary self-dual code, four-negacirculant code 1 Introduction Self-dual codes are one of the most interesting classes of codes.

arxiv-2309-11958.title: Seeing dark matter via acceleration radiation
arxiv-2309-11958.creator: Syed Masood A. S. Bukhari 1, Li-Gang Wang 1
arxiv-2309-11958.description: Abstract Despite constituting a noteworthy ∼ 27 % \sim 27\% share of the total energy budget of our Universe, dark matter (DM) has thus far eluded direct observations. Owing to its pervasive nature, there is a sincere expectation that astrophysical black holes (BHs) encompassed by DM should leave distinctive imprints on the gravitational waves arising from BH mergers.

arxiv-2403-11388.title: Traffic Weaver: semi-synthetic time-varying traffic generator based on averaged time series Journal: SoftwareX
arxiv-2403-11388.creator: Piotr Lechowicz, Aleksandra Knapińska, Adam Włodarczyk, Krzysztof Walkowiak
arxiv-2403-11388.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Piotr Lechowicz, Aleksandra Knapińska, Adam Włodarczyk, Krzysztof Walkowiak. Traffic Weaver is a Python package developed to generate a semi-synthetic signal (time series) with finer granularity, based on averaged time series, in a manner that, upon averaging, closely matches the original signal provided. The key components utilized to recreate the signal encompass oversampling with a given strategy, stretching to match the integral of the original time series, smoothing, repeating, applying trend, and adding noise.

arxiv-2504-12246.title: Branching Bisimulation Learning
arxiv-2504-12246.creator: Alessandro Abate, Mirco Giacobbe, Christian Micheletti, Yannik Schnitzer
arxiv-2504-12246.description: Abstract We introduce a bisimulation learning algorithm for non-deterministic transition systems. We generalise bisimulation learning to systems with bounded branching and extend its applicability to model checking branching-time temporal logic, while previously it was limited to deterministic systems and model checking linear-time properties.

arxiv-2507-02316.description: Abstract . Text-to-video (T2V) synthesis has advanced rapidly, yet current evaluation metrics primarily capture visual quality and temporal consistency, offering limited insight into how synthetic videos perform in downstream tasks such as text-to-video retrieval (TVR). In this work, we introduce SynTVA, a new dataset and benchmark designed to evaluate the utility of synthetic videos for building retrieval models.

arxiv-2507-15846.title: GUI-G 2 : Gaussian Reward Modeling for GUI Grounding
arxiv-2507-15846.creator: Fei Tang 1,2 , Zhangxuan Gu 2 , Zhengxi Lu 1 , Xuyang Liu 2 Shuheng Shen 2 , Changhua Meng 2 , Wen Wang 1 , Wenqi Zhang 1 Yongliang Shen 1 , Weiming Lu 1 , Jun Xiao 1 , Yueting Zhuang 1 1 Zhejiang University, 2 Ant Group {flysugar, syl}@zju.edu.cn shuheng.ssh@antgroup.com GitHub: https://github.com/
arxiv-2507-15846.description: Abstract Graphical User Interface (GUI) grounding maps natural language instructions to precise interface locations for autonomous interaction. Current reinforcement learning approaches use binary rewards that treat elements as hit-or-miss targets, creating sparse signals that ignore the continuous nature of spatial interactions.

arxiv-2509-19655.title: A Better-Than- 5 / 4 5/4 -Approximation for Two-Edge Connectivity
arxiv-2509-19655.creator: Felix Hommelsheim, Alexander Lindermayr, Zhenwei Liu
arxiv-2509-19655.description: Abstract The 2-Edge-Connected Spanning Subgraph Problem (2ECSS) is a fundamental problem in survivable network design. Given an undirected 2 2 -edge-connected graph, the goal is to find a 2 2 -edge-connected spanning subgraph with the minimum number of edges; a graph is 2-edge-connected if it is connected after the removal of any single edge.

arxiv-2602-13455.title: Using Machine Learning to Enhance the Detection of Obfuscated Abusive Words in Swahili: A Focus on Child Safety
arxiv-2602-13455.creator: Phyllis Nabangi, Abdul-Jalil Zakaria, Jema David Ndibwile
arxiv-2602-13455.description: Abstract The rise of digital technology has dramatically increased the potential for cyberbullying and online abuse, necessitating enhanced measures for detection and prevention, especially among children. This study focuses on detecting abusive obfuscated language in Swahili, a low-resource language that poses unique challenges due to its limited linguistic resources and technological support.

pmc-13328929.creator: Ilona Ruotsalainen, Carolynn Patten, Timo Niemirepo, Juha Pajula, Heidi Similä, Milla Immonen
pmc-13328929.description: Gait impairments are a well-documented consequence of stroke, yet the impact of transient ischemic attack (TIA) on gait remains underexplored.
